title: Tiered eval thresholds and A/B failback playbook for Optimize
creator: Marisol Reyes
description:
Goal: Produce a prescriptive PRD and runbook that defines tiered quality thresholds, statistical A/B acceptance criteria, and automated/manual rollback/playback behaviors for Optimize eval deployments. This ticket consolidates product requirements, acceptance criteria, and operational steps so Engineering and SRE can implement automated guardrails and Console indicators for canaries and full rollouts.

Background: Optimize runs continuous evals on model changes using prompt sets and metric ensembles. Current practice relies on ad-hoc thresholds and manual decision-making during rollouts. We need a repeatable policy that balances sensitivity to real regressions with minimizing false positives that unnecessarily block deployment.

Scope (in):
- Define a tiered signal taxonomy (green/yellow/red) across key signals (semantic quality, hallucination, safety, latency, token-cost).
- Specify per-signal numerical thresholds and short/medium/long windows for automated checks.
- Define A/B test statistical criteria (minimum n, significance, MDE, stopping rules) for candidate model rollouts within Optimize.
- Design an automated canary cadence and failback policy (percentages, monitoring windows, automatic pause/fallback).
- Produce acceptance criteria and test plan for engineering to implement.

Scope (out):
- Changes to model training pipelines or prompt engineering playbooks (only detects regressions).
- New human-labeling tooling (we will reference existing ops).

Success criteria:
- A single doc with clear thresholds and a runnable playbook that Engineering can implement as policy configs for canary jobs and A/B endpoints.
- Console exposes colored state for canaries and a clear recommended action with links.
- Automation covers "pause rollout" and "auto-fallback to previous stable model" for high-severity regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Document published in Confluence and linked from the Optimize PRD
Tiered thresholds (green/yellow/red) specified for at least 5 signals with numerical bounds and evaluation windows
A/B criteria include min sample size, primary metric, statistical test and stopping rules; documented MDE and alpha/beta choices
Rollout plan enumerates percentages (0, 5, 25, 100), monitoring windows, and automated actions for each tier
Engineering can wire the policy as configuration (no hard-coded thresholds in service code) and validation tests pass
Runbook contains an incident checklist and Slack/gating hooks; on-call SRE can follow steps to rollback within 15 minutes
eval_signals: Semantic-quality: Top-line similarity-to-reference using embedding-based ranking + human-labeled Likert (0-5)
Hallucination-rate: fraction of answers flagged by heuristics and confirmed by sampled human review
Safety-toxicity: scored by internal safety classifier (0-1) and external third-party check
Token-cost-per-request: mean total tokens billed per request
tiered_thresholds: Green (OK): Semantic-quality delta from baseline >= -0.5% over 24h; Hallucination change <= +0.2pp (absolute) over 24h; Safety regression none; Latency p95 <= baseline + 15%

Yellow (attention): Semantic-quality delta between -0.5% and -2.0% over 24-72h; Hallucination increase between +0.2pp and +1.0pp; Safety score degradation < 0.05 absolute; Latency p95 between +15% and +40%
Red (block): Semantic-quality delta < -2.0% over 24h OR Hallucination increase > +1.0pp OR Safety degradation >= 0.05 absolute OR Latency p95 > baseline + 40%
Threshold windows: short window = 1h (alerting), medium = 24h (canary gating), long = 72h (release rollback evaluation)
ab_criteria: Primary metric: task-weighted composite score (combined semantic-quality and hallucination penalty)
Statistical test: two-sided bootstrap with control for multiple comparisons across prompt strata; default alpha=0.01 for safety-critical signals, alpha=0.05 otherwise
Minimum sample size: computed per-stratum to achieve MDE=1% on composite score; fall back to global minimum N=5,000 per variant if stratum calc not available
Stopping rules: sequential testing with pre-specified alpha spending; require consistent sign for 2 consecutive monitoring windows before direct rollback unless red-level safety triggers fire
Confidence intervals and p-values surfaced in Console; do not accept rollout if lower bound of treated-control delta <= -MDE
rollback_triggers: Immediate auto-rollback: any red-level safety regression (toxicity increase) confirmed by automated pipeline = rollback to previous model and page on-call
Auto-pause canary: red-level semantic or hallucination regression observed within the canary window triggers automatic pause and reversion to previous traffic split
Manual-intervene: yellow-level sustained for >72h escalates to PM/Engineering for manual decision; recommended actions documented

Gradual-fallback: if cost or latency regressions cross yellow but not red, automatically reduce traffic to 25% while alerting SRE; if persists another monitoring window, reduce to 0% and flag for rollback
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Shadow run against 100% traffic but no production serving for 24h; collect full eval metrics
Phase 1: Canary at 5% traffic for 2 monitoring windows (each window=1h); require green or yellow-only signals to proceed
Phase 2: Ramp to 25% for 6 monitoring windows (6h); require no new red-level signals and A/B checks stable
Phase 3: Ramp to 100% with continued monitoring and an automated 72h rapid-rollback guard
During every phase: run targeted human review sampling for safety-sensitive prompt strata (10-50 samples per window)
test_plan: Unit tests for threshold evaluation logic and alert-trigger translation
Integration test: synthetic canary runs with injected regressions (safety, hallucination, latency) to verify automated pause/rollback behaviors
A/B simulation: replay historical traffic and bootstrap resampling to validate sample size calculations and false positive rates
End-to-end dry run: execute a mock rollout in staging using Console pipelines and verify escalation links, dashboards, and runbook instructions
Post-deploy validation: 100-sample human audit after each Phase 2->3 transition to confirm no unobserved regressions
updates: 2025-07-09: Kickoff sync with Eng + SRE. Agreed to parametrize thresholds and avoid hard-coding. Assigned ENG owners for each dependency.
2025-07-12: Safety review requested from Research; they recommended lowering alpha for toxicity tests to 0.01. Incorporated into A/B criteria.
2025-07-15: UX reviewed initial runbook; asked for one-click rollback link and clearer guidance for PM escalation — added to rollbook actions.
2025-07-18: SRE asked to add an automated traffic-reduction step (25% fallback) for yellow-level latency regressions; updated rollback logic.
2025-07-22: Finalized thresholds for initial implementation; awaiting ENG-4312 merge to begin integration testing.
notes: Tradeoffs: tighter thresholds reduce risk but increase false positives. We selected conservative red thresholds and a yellow state for human-in-the-loop assessment.
Open question: whether to use parametric tests for small prompt strata or always bootstrap; engineering prefers bootstrap for robustness.
Follow-ups: define post-rollback incident blameless postmortem template and integrate with Console incident links.
